chart.reason: The dataset is a 62-year structured time series — quantitative comparison is the entire point of the story.

image.reason: Three atmospheric editorial images anchor the three eras of the story (the world, China's rise, the private layer). They break analytical density and give the page emotional contour.

video.reason: No specific event-of-the-moment to dramatise — the story is structural over decades, not a single launch event. A 5s clip would feel decorative.

audio.reason: Space launches have a sonic dimension in real life, but a generic generated soundscape would be decorative. A meaningful sonification (e.g. one tone per launch year) would not aid comprehension here. Skipped intentionally.

interactive_or_map.reason: The annual-by-state series rewards exploration; a hover-able multi-line chart lets readers find their own country and trace its history. We also use a guess-first reveal for the 2018 leaderboard.

des_teaser.label: Teaser hero image — twilight launch

content.prompt: Cinematic editorial hero image of a single rocket launching at twilight against a deep navy sky, contrails twisting upward, distant horizon glow, faint silhouettes of multiple launch towers in the background suggesting a global industry, no text in frame, dramatic lighting, ultra wide shot, photographic realism

des_teaser.brief: Full-bleed dark cinematic image at the top of the page. A single rocket leaves a curling contrail against deep navy twilight; in the distance multiple launch towers are dimly visible — the visual cue that this is a globally crowded industry, not a two-superpower contest.
des_teaser.rationale: Sets the tone (dark editorial, restrained) and previews the core claim — a multi-actor space industry — without spelling it out.

des_01.label: 2018 leaderboard — guess-first reveal

content.initial_state: Three buttons: 'United States', 'Russia', 'China'. Prompt: 'Who launched the most orbital rockets in 2018?'
content.trigger: Reader clicks one of the three states.
content.transition: After click, the chosen state highlights, then a horizontal bar chart fades in showing 2018 successes per state with the actual answer (China = 28) emphasised in red. A caption appears beneath: 'For the first time, China launched more than anyone else.'
content.payoff: Most readers will pick US or Russia from intuition — the reveal makes the leaderboard land emotionally, not just visually.

des_01.brief: A guess-first interactive that opens the piece. The reader commits to a prediction before seeing the bar chart. After the click, a clean horizontal bar chart fades in with all six 2018 states shown — China highlighted in red, others in muted grey — and a one-line caption confirms the headline finding.
des_01.rationale: The lead finding is genuinely counter-intuitive for a general reader; a guess-first reveal converts a chart into a discovery. Matches the editor's 'lead with the surprise' direction.

des_02.label: All-time launches by state — ranked bar

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing exact count and pct

des_02.brief: Horizontal bar chart of all 14 launching states across the entire 1957-2018 record. Russia/USSR is so far ahead it dominates the chart — that visual disparity IS the point. Bars are muted grey except RU/SU and US which are tinted to flag the duopoly era.
des_02.rationale: A ranked bar shows the all-time concentration cleanly without relying on percent labels.

des_03.label: Annual launches by major state — multi-line

content.interaction: hover any line for year + state value tooltip

des_03.brief: The piece's analytical centrepiece. A multi-line chart spanning 1957-2018 with six states colour-coded. Three vertical annotations mark the Soviet peak (1982), the dissolution (1991), and the China overtake (2018). Readers can trace any country across the full era.
des_03.rationale: Trend chart is the clearest mode for the year-by-year structural arc; this is exactly the chart The Economist's original article centred on.

des_04.label: Soviet collapse stat callout

content.label: drop in Russian launches from the 1982 peak to the late 1990s

des_04.brief: Large stat callout: 4.0× in display weight, with caption explaining the 1982 peak (101) and the 1996-2000 mean (25.2).
des_04.rationale: Concentrates one of the strongest narrative beats into a single number.

des_05.label: China launch pad scene

content.prompt: Editorial photograph of a Long March rocket on its launch pad in China at dusk, golden gantry lights, scaffolding and umbilicals visible, vapour curling off cryogenic tanks, dramatic low-angle perspective looking up, deep blue twilight sky, no text in frame, photojournalism aesthetic

des_05.brief: Atmospheric editorial photo of a Long March-style launcher on the pad at dusk. Conveys the new third pole — a working, well-funded Chinese launch industry — without flag-waving.
des_05.rationale: The China-overtake section needs visual presence; a real-feeling rocket scene grounds the abstraction.

des_06.label: Cumulative launches — area chart

content.interaction: hover for cumulative count at any year

des_06.brief: Cumulative-launch line chart with three lines (RU/SU, US, CN). Russia stays far above, US plateaus, China has the steepest recent slope. End-of-line labels show 3,024 / 1,585 / 289.
des_06.rationale: Cumulative chart shows the absolute gap; the slope difference shows the convergence story.

des_07.label: Decadal launches by major state — small multiples

content.interaction: hover for state x decade tooltip

des_07.brief: Compact grouped bar chart showing each decade as a cluster, with bars for US, RU/SU, CN, F, J, IN. The 1980s Soviet bar dwarfs everything; the 2010s shows three bars of similar height for the first time.
des_07.rationale: Pairs with des_06 — the cumulative chart shows absolute lead, the decadal grouped bar shows convergence.

des_08.label: Private launch — drone ship landing

content.prompt: Editorial documentary photograph of a SpaceX-style sleek white booster touching down vertically on an ocean drone-ship at dawn, four landing legs deployed, faint engine glow, calm Atlantic horizon, soft dawn light, atmospheric haze, no text in frame, hyperrealistic photographic style

des_08.brief: Iconic vertical-landing image. The single best visual anchor for 'private firms now do what only states used to do'.
des_08.rationale: The private-rocket transition is half the story; a real-feeling landing image gives that section the same visual weight as the China section.

des_09.label: Agency-type share over time — stacked area
des_09.brief: 100% stacked area chart showing the relentless rise of private and startup launches as share of all orbital launches, in 5-year buckets from 1955 to 2018. State drops from 100% to ~50%; startup carves out 15.2% by 2015-18.
des_09.rationale: Stacked area makes the structural transition visible — the eye reads share, not absolute count.

des_10.label: SpaceX trajectory — bar chart
des_10.brief: Compact bar chart showing SpaceX successes 2008-2018: 1,1,2,0,2,3,6,6,8,18,17. Annotation on the 2017 bar marks the inflection.
des_10.rationale: A small inset chart embedded in the private-launch section drives home the company-level scale of the transition.

des_11.label: Failure rate by decade — line
des_11.brief: Steep declining line from 53.85% in the 1950s to 2.94% in the 1980s, with a small plateau through 2010s. End-points labelled with their percent value and the underlying total/failure counts in tooltip.
des_11.rationale: A line chart makes the engineering-maturity trend immediately readable.

des_12.label: Top 10 vehicle families — horizontal bar
des_12.brief: Top 10 vehicle families ranked by total flights. Eight of ten are Russian (red tint); only Space Shuttle and one other are tinted American blue. Soyuz-U at 632 dominates.
des_12.rationale: Quick color tinting communicates the Russian-engineering dominance without a separate explanatory chart.

des_13.label: Closing stat strip

content.label: of 2018 launches were flown by private firms or startups

des_13.brief: Closing oversized stat that pairs the 'China leads' opener with the 'private firms fly half' close. Sets up the final paragraph.
des_13.rationale: Bookends the piece — opens on geography (China), closes on operator type (private).

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial — deep navy background with soft white text and selective accent colour for highlights
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: alternating image-then-chart-then-text, never two charts in a row without a non-chart break
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Skip the standard click-to-play audio card. Use a guess-first interactive instead of a passive lead chart. Pair three atmospheric photographs (twilight launch, China pad, private landing) instead of a single hero image — the three eras of the story get equal visual weight.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Headline serif at 56-72px, body sans-serif, large stat callouts at 80px, soft horizontal hairlines as section dividers, generous vertical spacing between sections.
